description: What the cost suite must notice about catalog estimates: the catalog overrides the owner's rates, an estimate is not marked as one, a tier is applied at the wrong size or not at all, the wrong tier is chosen, a missing cache rate is read as free, an estimate is refused for want of a cache split, the ledger forgets its estimates, or an absurd catalog price is accepted.

mutations.name: K1
mutations.what: the catalog's rates are used even when the owner supplied rates

mutations.name: K2
mutations.what: a price made from the catalog is not marked as an estimate

mutations.name: K3
mutations.what: a prompt of exactly the size of a tier is priced at the tier (the rule is "more than")

mutations.name: K4
mutations.what: the tiers of the catalog are never applied

mutations.name: K5
mutations.what: the first tier the prompt is over is used, not the highest

mutations.name: K6
mutations.what: a cache read rate the catalog does not list is taken as free

mutations.name: K7
mutations.what: an estimate is refused when the provider did not report the cache split (as the owner's rates are)

mutations.name: K8
mutations.what: the ledger does not count the responses it priced from the catalog

mutations.name: K9
mutations.what: an absurd price in the catalog is accepted

mutations.name: K10
mutations.what: the sum over several conversations forgets the estimates

mutations.name: K11
mutations.what: a saved ledger forgets how many of its responses were estimates

mutations.name: K12
mutations.what: a cache write rate the catalog does not list is taken as free
